 Automation systems 
 Safe migration of automation systems 
 How can we support the automation system migration process? 
 Contact us 
 The migration of industrial automation systems is not only about replacing outdated hardware, but above all about strategically unlocking the potential of data and increasing the company’s operational resilience.
 Migration What do we gain from migration? 
 Increased efficiency and cost reduction
 Modern automation systems deliver higher performance, improved reliability and less production downtime. Migration cuts maintenance costs, simplifies infrastructure management, and enables advanced diagnostics and optimization.
 Higher cybersecurity standards
 Legacy systems are the primary targets of cyberattacks. Migration provides access to preventive and adaptive cybersecurity, including data encryption and advanced threat detection mechanisms.
 Integration with modern technologies (IT/OT)
 The possibility of implementing new technologies such as AI, supporting decision-making on the shop floor. Edge and cloud computing: modern systems enable data processing closer to the source (edge), reducing latency.
 Sustainability and environmental protection
 Modernization enables the measurement and optimization of energy consumption and carbon footprint, which is essential for maintaining competitiveness. Extending lifecycle of existing assets through modernization (retrofitting).
 Availability of spare parts and support
 Maintaining systems from the 1980s or 1990s is becoming increasingly difficult and costly due to the lack of spare parts and diminishing manufacturer support. Migration to modern platforms ensures operational stability.
 Select the system you want to migrate

 SIMATIC S7-1200 – end of lifecycle for the first generation and the recommended solution for the future 
 Siemens announces that the first generation of SIMATIC S7-1200 controllers (G1) will begin its gradual phase-out process as of November 1, 2026.
 More on Support Industry 
 At the same time, the successor controller, SIMATIC S7-1200 G2 , has been introduced to the portfolio – a modern generation of controllers designed to meet the future requirements of industrial automation.
 Learn about SIMATIC S7‑1200 G2 
 Key dates – SIMATIC S7-1200 (G1) 
 01.11.2026 
 – official announcement of product phase-out
 Until 31.10.2027 – possibility to order G1 as a new device
 Until approx. 2036 – planned availability of modules as spare parts
 ➡ Customers can safely plan the completion of current projects and the maintenance of existing installations.
 SIMATIC S7-1200 G2 – recommended solution for new projects 
 SIMATIC S7-1200 G2 is the natural successor to G1, offering tangible business and technical benefits:
✅ Higher performance and scalability – shorter cycle times, greater application capabilities
✅ Modern machine safety – optimized Safety portfolio compliant with current standards
✅ Enhanced Motion Control functions (previously unavailable in S7-1200) – improved precision and application dynamics
✅ Ready for digitalization – greater data transparency, support for digitalization and resource efficiency
✅ Industrial-grade cybersecurity – compliance with IEC 62443-4-2
✅ Full integration with TIA Portal – engineering continuity and faster project deployment

 Copilot said: SIMATIC S7-300 Controllers → S7-1500 Controllers 
 SIMATIC S7-300 together with the ET 200M I/O system was discontinued on October 1, 2025 (product phase-out status PM410 – Product Removed from Portfolio). The successor to this discontinued product family is the SIMATIC S7-1500 system, together with the SIMATIC ET 200MP and ET 200SP distributed I/O modules, the SIMATIC S7-400 system, and the SIMATIC ET 200SP HA distributed I/O system (Process Automation).Further details can be found in the announcement on the global support website: “Information about the product phase-out of S7-300 / ET 200M components” 
 See full announcement 
 After this date, S7-300 system components can only be purchased as spare parts or returned for repair. We reserve the right to supply certain components exclusively on an exchange basis for defective parts. Please note that components can only be ordered in the standard quantities applicable to spare parts. The supply of components for the expansion of existing installations or for the construction of new systems is not possible.
 For this reason, migration of existing systems to the recommended solutions based on the newer SIMATIC S7-1500 product family is strongly recommended. The PM490 status, which represents the end of production and sales of the S7-300 system , is scheduled for October 1, 2033 . If a specific quantity of such components is required beyond the PM490 phase, it is generally possible to enter into an individual long-term agreement in advance. In such cases, technical support, repair services, and parts availability can only be guaranteed under the terms of a separate individual agreement.
 Signal Adapters 
 Signal adapters for I/O modules of legacy systems enable fast and reliable migration to the latest technology standards. Benefits of using signal adapters: 
 Hardware engineering costs are kept low, as only the controller needs to be replaced. All existing field wiring remains in place.
 No revisions to electrical schematics are required; signal lists are automatically updated by the engineering software.
 Production downtime is significantly reduced.
 This approach not only saves time and money but also substantially minimizes the risk of errors.
 Interface Module Adapter

This tool enables you to prepare a file that can be imported into the latest version of TIA Portal , based on the original source project.

 SIMATIC Comfort HMI Panels → Unified Comfort HMI Panels 
 As of January 2026, a phase-out process for Comfort Panels has been announced. They will remain available for purchase as new devices until the end of December 2027.
 Check availability 
 For several years, the innovative WinCC Unified visualization system family has been under development, including the Unified Comfort panel equivalents. As the architectures of the two systems differ, direct migration of visualizations between them is not possible. To simplify this process as much as possible, Siemens has developed dedicated engineering tools to support migration.These tools can also be used to migrate from HMI Basic 2nd generation to Unified Basic, as well as from WinCC Runtime Advanced to WinCC Runtime Unified.
 Modernization Guide 
 In the modernization guide, you will find information on how to properly approach upgrading your visualization system to Unified. The step-by-step guide highlights the differences between the old and the new system, shows where to start, and which tools to use to make the process as effective as possible.
 Learn more 
 Modernization Checker 
 A tool for analyzing HMI Comfort, Basic 2nd generation, or WinCC Advanced projects. After generating a report, you will learn which functions will require a different approach in the Unified system, along with references to documentation explaining how to handle them. The report will also identify areas that cannot currently be directly transferred. Additionally, it includes a checklist to help track progress during the modernization process.
 Learn more 
 Data2Unified 
 As visualizations in Basic 2nd generation, Comfort, and WinCC Advanced systems are based on a different architecture than WinCC Unified, direct copying of objects between these systems is not possible. This transfer is enabled by the Data2Unified tool, built on TIA Portal Openness. Use it to transfer most data, objects, screens, and their properties to the Unified system.

 SINAMICS V90 Drives → SINAMICS S200 Drives 
 SINAMICS V90 replaced by SINAMICS S200 
 SINAMICS V90 Is Being Discontinued. Meet Its Successor – SINAMICS S200
 Starting October 1, 2026, Siemens will begin the phase-out process of the SINAMICS V90 servo drive system in regions outside China. This solution, which has been widely used for years in applications requiring precise positioning and reliable motion control, will gradually be replaced by the modern SINAMICS S200 servo drive system.SINAMICS S200 represents the next generation of standard Siemens servo drives. The system consists of the SINAMICS S200 drive, SIMOTICS S-1FL2 motors, and MOTION-CONNECT 350 / 380 cables. For new applications and planned machine upgrades, we recommend considering SINAMICS S200 already at the project concept stage.
 PLM Status
 Successor 
 Recommendation 
 P.M400 – Product Discontinuation Announcement: October 1, 2025
 P.M410 – Product Cancellation: October 1, 2026
 SINAMICS S200 + SIMOTICS S-1FL2 + MOTION-CONNECT 350 / 380
 Plan all new projects and modernization activities using SINAMICS S200.
 Why SINAMICS S200?
 SINAMICS S200 has been designed as a standard single-axis AC/AC servo drive system for motion control applications. Compared to SINAMICS V90, it offers a more modern architecture, higher dynamics, easier commissioning, and greater readiness for digitalization.
 Higher dynamics and precision: Faster control loop cycles and PROFINET RT/IRT communication down to 250 µs in PN variants.
 TIA Portal integration: Commissioning and diagnostics via Startdrive, plus convenient operation through the integrated web server.
 Simplified selection and commissioning: One Button Tuning, automatic drive identification, and an electronic motor nameplate.
 Compact design: Reduced installation space requirements and easier cabinet layout.
 Safety Integrated: STO (Safe Torque Off) certified up to SIL3 for standard safety applications.
 System-wide integration: Drive, motor, cables, and engineering tools form a consistent and straightforward migration solution. 
 What Does the Phase-Out of SINAMICS V90 Mean for Users?
 Products from the SINAMICS V90 family will gradually move through the subsequent stages of the Siemens Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) process.
 For existing installations, users should verify spare parts availability, article number status, and service plans through the latest information available in Siemens Industry Online Support and SiePortal.
 For new applications and planned modernization projects, migration to SINAMICS S200 is recommended.
 Migration planning should begin early, as the replacement selection process should take into account power rating, supply voltage, communication version, motor inertia, cable configuration, brake requirements, and specific application demands.

 Migration: What Should Be Prepared Before Selecting a Replacement?
 When replacing SINAMICS V90 with SINAMICS S200, it is advisable to collect the key application data in advance. This helps avoid incorrect sizing and reduces the time required to prepare a technical proposal.
 MLFB numbers of the existing drive, motor, and cables.
 Supply voltage and axis power rating
 Communication version: PROFINET or Pulse Train Input (PTI).
 Required motor type and inertia class: low, medium, or high inertia.
 Requirements for brake, cables, cable lengths, and installation conditions.
 TIA Portal / Startdrive version used in the engineering environment.
 Application requirements: positioning, speed, torque, vertical axis operation, measurement functions, homing, and safety requirements.

 Need Assistance with Migration? 
 Contact your local Siemens representative or technical support team. We can help select the right SINAMICS S200 replacement, verify application data, configure the drive in TIA Portal, and prepare a smooth migration and modernization plan.

 Systems SIMOTION -> SIMATIC S7-1500T 
 The Future of Motion Control Begins Today
 The SIMATIC S7-1500T combines PLC, Motion Control, Safety, Diagnostics, and HMI functions in a single engineering environment, the TIA Portal. This is a natural modernization path for SIMOTION-based machines.
 For over 20 years, SIMOTION has been one of the most advanced and respected Motion Control systems on the market. Thanks to the tight integration of PLC, drive, and motion functions, it has enabled the implementation of thousands of demanding machine applications worldwide.
 Currently, Siemens is consistently developing a strategy based on SIMATIC S7-1500T technology controllers, which adopt and even extend Motion Control functionality, providing greater flexibility and full integration in the TIA Portal environment.
 Why Migrate from SIMOTION?
 Single Engineering Environment
 T-CPU controllers utilize the TIA Portal platform, integrating in a single project:
• PLC,
• Motion Control functions,
• SINAMICS drives,
• Safety Integrated safety systems,
• Diagnostics,
• HMI, and SCADA.
 This provides users with a single, consistent design environment that shortens machine commissioning, maintenance, and expansion times.
 Modern Hardware Architecture
SIMATIC S7-1500T controllers provide high computing power, short cycle times, support for multiple synchronous axes, advanced kinematic functions, and readiness for future industrial communication.
 Simplified Maintenance
Control platform standardization reduces the number of spare parts, programming tools, and training, as well as reduces the risk associated with the availability of legacy components.
 The Most Important Benefit
Migration doesn't have to mean a revolution in the machine. A well-prepared plan allows you to maintain proven technological assumptions while simultaneously migrating the application to a current and evolving automation platform.
 What can be migrated?
Most SIMOTION-based applications can be ported to the T-CPU, including:
✓ Single axes
✓ Electronic gears
✓ Electronic cams
✓ Axis synchronization
✓ Positioning
✓ Flying Saw applications
✓ Rotary Knife applications
✓ Pick & Place systems
✓ Multi-axis servo systems
✓ Machine kinematics control
 SCALANCE industrial network components 
 SCALANCE Industrial Network Components Siemens industrial networks form the foundation of modern automation infrastructure, ensuring reliable, efficient, and secure communication between devices, machines, and IT/OT systems. Due to the evolution of the SCALANCE portfolio, some older devices have been retired or are being phased out. Siemens recommends migrating to the latest SCALANCE platforms, which offer higher performance, greater integration capabilities, and advanced cybersecurity features.
